newsitem.title: JAPAN: BOJ says policy geared towards economic recovery.
newsitem.headline: BOJ says policy geared towards economic recovery.

text.p: The Bank of Japan's monetary policy is geared towards ensuring a solid basis for economic recovery, BOJ Governor Yasuo Matsushita told a news conference on Wednesday.

"Japan's current economic recovery needs to strengthen further for it to become a self-sustainable process. It is necessary for the cycle of demand, production and income to become firmly established," Matsushita said.
"Monetary policy will continue to put emphasis on ensuring the basis for economic recovery, and it is appropriate that we keep close watch over financial and economic conditions," he added.
The central bank maintained its view that the Japanese economy is continuing on its gradual recovery track, he said.
"Recent economic data generally supports our view (on the economy)," Matsushita said.

He said corporate profits and sales are increasing among all industries and companies of various sizes, as seen in the BOJ's latest quarterly corporate survey, known as the "tankan", which was unveiled late last month.
The tankan also showed upward revisions in capital spending, he said.

Japan's April-June gross domestic product (GDP) data, announced late last week, confirmed that public works spending and housing investments are still at a high level, and that corporate capital spending is being carried out steadily, he said.
Although private consumption tends to fluctuate, it is still on a gradual improving trend, he added.
"The economic recovery is continuing steadily, but the pace of increase in production and capital spending shows that the pace of economic recovery is still gradual," he added.

An improvement in business sentiment has stalled for the moment, since inventory adjustments in the semiconductor industry and some other materials industries are being prolonged, and exports are declining, Matsushita said.
But there are favourable factors, such as progress in stock adjustments in the steel industry, and a halt in the sluggishness of exports as a result of the yen's weakness.
The governor said the central bank's monetary policy would not be directly affected by a government decision on whether to adopt a supplementary budget to stimulate the economy in 1996/97.
